\[
\log_x w = 24 \Rightarrow \ln x = \frac{\ln w}{24}, \qquad
\log_y w = 40 \Rightarrow \ln y = \frac{\ln w}{40}
\]

Also,
\[
\log_{xyz} w = 12 \Rightarrow \ln(xyz) = \frac{\ln w}{12}
\]

Since \(\ln(xyz)=\ln x+\ln y+\ln z\),
\[
\ln z=\ln(xyz)-\ln x-\ln y
=\ln w\left(\frac1{12}-\frac1{24}-\frac1{40}\right)
=\ln w\left(\frac1{60}\right)
\]

Thus
\[
\log_z w=\frac{\ln w}{\ln z}=60
\]

\[
\boxed{60}
\]
